effects.evidenceText: Benton PUD lists manufactured-home rebate ranges and states homes must be electrically heated and in its service territory.

edgeActions.reason: The source funds certified manufactured homes or pre-1976 manufactured home replacement, not standalone high-efficiency HVAC replacement.

repairs.evidenceText: Benton PUD publishes manufactured-home rebate ranges, with electric-heating, service-territory, and six-month application requirements.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Do not expose as an HVAC replacement rebate even though certified homes include efficient building systems.

repairs.opportunityName: Richland Energy Services - Energy Efficient Commercial Lighting Program

effects.formulaText: For commercial lighting, select the applicable BPA Online Lighting Calculator measure and multiply the published per-lamp, per-tube, per-fixture, per-control, or $0.25/kWh-saved incentive by qualifying units or savings. Apply caps and requirements: incentive cannot exceed 70% of total project cost and BPA lighting incentives are also capped at $0.50/kWh saved; Richland requires preapproval, inspection, at least 30% wattage reduction, and simple payback of at least one year before incentive.
requiredInputs: fixture, lamp, tube, or control quantity
annual kWh savings for calculated measures
RES written approval before purchase or work begins
missingInputsForTypicalRetroFiEstimate: fixture, lamp, tube, or control quantity

measureCatalog.selectionInput: Select the BPA OLC lighting measure series, then provide wattage range, wattage-reduction tier, quantity, or annual kWh savings as required by the measure.

effects.evidenceText: Richland requires preapproval and uses BPA OLC lighting calculations. BPA's current offerings publish fixture, lamp, tube, controls, and kWh-saved rates, subject to project-cost and kWh-saved caps.

edgeActions.reason: Official Richland commercial and industrial program materials support lighting incentives for nonresidential accounts, and BPA OLC publishes LED lighting measure rates used for calculation.

stackingRules.notes: Lighting incentive cannot exceed 70% of total project cost. Source materials did not state broader stacking rules.

repairs.evidenceText: Richland offers nonresidential lighting rebates, requires application approval before work, completion within 120 days, at least 30% wattage reduction, and caps lighting incentives at 70% of total project cost.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Input target data reviewed from uploaded batch prompt. LED lighting is source-backed, but value must be calculated through BPA OLC measure rates and project-specific inputs.

repairs.opportunityName: Tax Abatement for Solar Manufacturers

effects.formulaText: For qualifying Washington solar energy system or component manufacturing, processing for hire, or wholesale sales, compute B&O tax at the preferential solar energy classification rate of 0.275% of taxable gross receipts. The tax benefit equals the difference between tax under the otherwise applicable B&O classification and tax under the 0.275% solar energy classification, after applicable deductions or multiple-activities tax credit adjustments.
ineligibleCostCategories: end-use rooftop solar PV installation costs
requiredInputs: deductions for interstate or foreign sales
Annual Tax Performance Report filing status

rows.activity: Manufacturing of solar energy systems or qualifying components
Wholesaling of solar energy systems or qualifying components

effects.evidenceText: Washington DOR states qualifying solar manufacturers, processors for hire, and wholesalers use preferential B&O classifications at 0.275%, with annual performance reporting required.

edgeActions.reason: The official DOR source applies to solar energy system and component manufacturers, processors for hire, and wholesalers, not to property owners installing rooftop solar PV.

stackingRules.notes: This is a preferential B&O tax classification for qualifying business activity, not a project rebate. DOR discusses deductions and multiple activities tax credit adjustments for B&O reporting.

timingRequirements.applicationDeadline: Preferential solar manufacturing and wholesaling B&O classifications expire July 1, 2032.

repairs.evidenceText: Washington DOR's solar manufacturing guidance describes preferential B&O tax classifications for qualifying manufacturers, processors for hire, and wholesalers, expiring July 1, 2032.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The opportunity is a business tax-rate preference and should not be exposed as a rooftop solar PV retrofit incentive.

repairs.opportunityName: Commercial Retro-Commissioning and New Construction Program

effects.formulaText: For Retro-Commissioning, verified EUI reduction of at least 3% earns a base incentive of $0.06/ft² plus $0.01/ft² for each additional 1% EUI reduction above 3%, capped at 15% EUI reduction or $0.18/ft². A $0.02/ft² RSP bonus may be passed to the customer if measures are implemented within 15 months. Incentives are capped at 75% of total audit plus implementation cost and the base incentive is capped at $100,000 per project.
eligibleCostCategories: implementation cost for qualifying energy-saving measures
missingInputsForTypicalRetroFiEstimate: project-level and customer annual incentive totals
effects.evidenceText: Focus on Energy's 2026 Retro-Commissioning application publishes EUI-reduction incentives from $0.06 to $0.18/ft², optional $0.02/ft² RSP bonus, and 75% cost cap.

effects.formulaText: Focus on Energy provides building optimization assistance for existing facilities and new construction or renovation support during design or construction. Non-cash assistance includes identifying and implementing operational changes or design strategies; any new construction financial incentive is project-specific and determined through Focus analysis and verification.
requiredInputs: energy model or online analysis inputs
effects.evidenceText: Focus describes building optimization and new construction support as technical and financial assistance; final new construction incentives depend on project analysis and verified savings.

edgeActions.reason: The official Focus on Energy building optimization path supports retro-commissioning studies for eligible existing buildings, with published 2026 incentive rates based on verified EUI reduction.

stackingRules.notes: Focus states a general project incentive limit of $300,000 per project and $400,000 per customer per calendar year across all Focus incentives; RCx base incentive also has a $100,000 project cap and 75% cost cap.

timingRequirements.applicationDeadline: Projects must be completed by 12/31/2026 for the cited 2026 Retro-Commissioning application.

repairs.evidenceText: Focus on Energy publishes a 2026 Retro-Commissioning incentive table based on verified EUI reduction and building square footage, plus separate process support for building optimization and new construction.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The retro-commissioning edge is supported as a nonphysical study/process measure. New construction design assistance should stay scoped as separate process support, not a single physical retrofit.

repairs.opportunityName: Madison Gas & Electric - Charge Ahead Program

effects.formulaText: For eligible MGE standard-rate residential EV customers, pay a monthly reward when the customer charges at least 80% off-peak during the calendar month, keeps smart charging enabled throughout the month, and has no more than three unmanaged sessions. Reward is $8 per month for June through August and $4 per month for September through May, for a maximum of $60 per year.
requiredInputs: smart charging enabled status for the full month
compatible EV or compatible home charger connection

rows.performanceRequirement: At least 80% off-peak charging, smart charging enabled throughout the month, and no more than three unmanaged sessions.
At least 80% off-peak charging, smart charging enabled throughout the month, and no more than three unmanaged sessions.

effects.evidenceText: MGE Charge Ahead pays standard-rate customers $8/month in June-August and $4/month in September-May if monthly smart-charging performance rules are met.

effects.formulaText: For eligible MGE time-of-use residential customers, Charge Ahead does not provide a separate cash reward. The app schedules charging to avoid peak periods and target lower-cost off-peak periods; bill savings depend on home EV charging kWh shifted from higher-cost to lower-cost TOU periods and the customer's applicable TOU rate differential.
requiredInputs: home EV charging kWh by time period
applicable on-peak and off-peak energy prices
missingInputsForTypicalRetroFiEstimate: home EV charging kWh by time period
effects.evidenceText: MGE says TOU customers do not receive cash incentives through Charge Ahead; savings come from shifting charging to lower-cost times on the bill.

edgeActions.reason: Official Charge Ahead materials state no charging station installation is required if the vehicle is supported; the source supports managed charging rewards, not charger purchase or installation rebates.

stackingRules.notes: No charger-installation rebate stacking rule was found because Charge Ahead is a managed charging reward and TOU optimization program.

repairs.evidenceText: MGE Charge Ahead is a residential managed charging program. Standard-rate customers can earn monthly rewards for off-peak smart charging; TOU customers receive bill savings rather than cash rewards.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The EV charger installation edge is unsupported. The calculable value is recurring performance reward for standard-rate customers and tariff-dependent savings for TOU customers.
